18	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
19	///
20	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
21	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
22	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
23	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
24	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
25	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
26	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
27	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
28	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
29	  case toolMissing(String)
30	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
31	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
32	  case authRequired(String)
33	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
34	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
35	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
36	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
37	  case noRemote
38	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
39	  case rejected(String)
40	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
41	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
42	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
43	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
44	  case rebaseInProgress
45	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
46	  ///
47	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
48	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
49	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
50	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
51	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
52	  ///
53	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
54	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
55	  ///
56	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
57	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
58	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
59	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
60	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
61	  /// jj refused to rewrite a commit protected by `immutable_heads()` — reached by Pull, whose
62	  /// `jj rebase -b @` moves the whole branch containing `@`, and that branch usually contains a
63	  /// remote-tracked commit. Measured on jj 0.43 for a workroom based off a feature branch while trunk
64	  /// moved on: `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`.
65	  ///
66	  /// Offers no retry, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the destination doesn't change between clicks, so
67	  /// every retry fails identically. The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base instead of
68	  /// guessing `trunk()` — filed, not built.
69	  case immutableHistory(String)
70	  /// jj refuses to push a commit with an empty description, changes or not. This is the state a workroom
71	  /// sits in the moment you edit a file and before you write a message, so it is the most reachable
72	  /// failure on the push path, not an edge case. Measured: `Error: Won't push commit 050e657d3c36 since
73	  /// it has no description`.
74	  case needsDescription(String)
75	  case other(String)
76	}

123	/// The seam for VCS operations that **write** — remote state reads plus fetch/push/pull.
124	///
125	/// Separate from `VCSProviding` on purpose. That protocol's doc calls it "the single seam the app
126	/// **reads** VCS data through", and four resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no
127	/// gate. Putting `fetch` there would mean nothing structurally prevented a read path from firing a
128	/// network mutation — the opposite of what `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee. Keeping writes on
129	/// their own protocol also gives the injected `StatusCommandRunning` a home: `GitProvider` and
130	/// `RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one.
131	///
132	/// This is the growth surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, bookmark management,
133	/// the deep jj ops), which is why it's a protocol with a factory rather than one standalone resolver —
134	/// otherwise each later operation re-derives repo kind and wires its own runner.
135	protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
136	  /// Everything the toolbar renders, as ONE coherent snapshot.
137	  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
138	  func fetch(path: String, projectRoot: String, remote: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
139	  /// `anonymousRevision` is used only by jj, and only when `@` carries no bookmark: it is the revision
140	  /// the auto-created `push-<change-id>` bookmark will point at. Compute it with
141	  /// `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)` — pushing a bare `@` fails when the
142	  /// working copy is empty and undescribed, which is the state a fresh workroom sits in. Ignored by git.
143	  func push(
144	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool,
145	    anonymousRevision: String
146	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
147	  func pullRebase(
148	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
149	    tracking: VCSTracking?
150	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
151	  /// Recover a workroom left mid-rebase. git only; a no-op for jj, whose rebase is atomic and
152	  /// `jj undo`-able.
153	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
154	}

175	/// `VCSWriting` over the real `git` / `jj` CLIs.
176	///
177	/// **Why the CLI and not the libraries.** SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass `NULL` for the options
178	/// struct that would carry `git_remote_callbacks.credentials`, so they have no credential path at all —
179	/// HTTPS authentication is impossible through them — and it has no `pull`. Shelling the real binaries
180	/// means the user's own credential helpers, SSH agent and config just work, which is the same bet the
181	/// status layer already makes with `gh`. jj has no Swift API for these at all.
182	///
183	/// Pure `static` arg-builders, parsers and classifiers carry all the semantics, so they are unit-tested
184	/// without spawning anything — the pattern `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` established for exactly
185	/// this reason.
186	///
187	/// ```
188	///                 ┌──────────── every network op ────────────┐
189	///                 │ runNetwork: stdin=/dev/null, BatchMode,   │
190	///                 │ askpass off, SSH_AUTH_SOCK forwarded      │
191	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
192	///                                      │
193	///                 ┌────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
194	///                 │  JJSnapshotGate.run(projectRoot:)         │  git writes too
195	///                 │  NEVER re-enter for the same root         │
196	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
197	///                                      │
198	///     git ─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────── jj
199	///  fetch → PROJECT ROOT (FETCH_HEAD    │   fetch → PROJECT ROOT (a workspace
200	///          is per-worktree; the root   │           has no .git)
201	///          is one shared answer)       │   push  → PROJECT ROOT (bookmarks are
202	///  push  → workroom                    │           repo-global)
203	///  pull  → root (fetch) + workroom     │   pull  → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
204	///  abort → workroom                    │
205	/// ```
206	struct CLIVCSWriter: VCSWriting, Sendable {
207	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"` — resolved once by `VCS.writer(for:)` so no method re-derives it.
208	  let vcs: String
209	  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
210	  /// For `currentRef` only. The app already has a canonical answer including jj `.ancestor` and git
211	  /// `.detached`; re-deriving it from `%(HEAD)` would lose both.
212	  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
213	  /// Serializes writes per project root. Applied to **git** as well as jj: a project's workrooms are
214	  /// `git worktree add` worktrees sharing one `.git`, so a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a
215	  /// workroom wedged in a rebase.
216	  let gate: JJSnapshotGate
217	
218	  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
219	  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
220	  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
221	  /// Generous because SIGKILLing a rebase is the one genuinely unsafe timeout here — it can leave
222	  /// `rebase-merge` behind. `classify` probes for that and reports `.rebaseInProgress`.
223	  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300
224	
225	  // MARK: - Placement
226	
227	  /// Where an operation must run.
228	  ///
229	  /// **fetch always runs at the project root, for both backends.** For jj because a secondary
230	  /// workspace has no `.git` (the rule `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory` already encodes for
231	  /// `gh`). For git because `FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree** — fetching inside a workroom would leave
232	  /// the project and every sibling workroom reading "never fetched" while their remote refs were
233	  /// perfectly fresh. At the root it's one fact every workroom of the project agrees on.
234	  ///
235	  /// **Everything except fetch runs in the workroom, including jj push.** It used to send jj push to the
236	  /// root on the grounds that bookmarks are repo-global. Bookmarks are — but `@` is not: it is
237	  /// WORKSPACE-scoped, resolved against the working directory. So `jj git push --change @` run at the root
238	  /// pushed the ROOT workspace's working copy and left the workroom's commit at home, while still
239	  /// returning `.ok` so the toolbar reported "Pushed to origin".
240	  ///
241	  /// Measured, root holding `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK` and workspace `wsA` holding `WORKROOM-WORK`: the push
242	  /// created `refs/heads/push-<root's change id>` carrying `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK`. Wrong commit published,
243	  /// the user's work never sent, success reported. `--bookmark` works from a secondary workspace too, so
244	  /// nothing needed the root.
245	  ///
246	  /// The integration test could not see this — it passes `path` and `projectRoot` as the same directory,
247	  /// which makes the two indistinguishable. `opDirectoryTests` now pins them as different.
248	  static func opDirectory(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, path: String, projectRoot: String) -> String {
249	    switch action {
250	    case .fetch: return projectRoot
251	    case .push, .pull, .abortRebase: return path
252	    }
253	  }

255	  /// The **common** git directory for a path — the one shared by every worktree of the repo.
256	  ///
257	  /// `.git` is a directory in a normal repo and a FILE in a worktree, containing
258	  /// `gitdir: <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>`. That per-worktree directory has its own `FETCH_HEAD`,
259	  /// `HEAD` and `index`, so reading `FETCH_HEAD` from it after fetching at the root finds nothing —
260	  /// the root's fetch wrote the root's copy. Stripping the `/worktrees/<name>` suffix gets the shared
261	  /// directory, which is where a root fetch's `FETCH_HEAD` actually lands.
262	  ///
263	  /// Pure string work, no subprocess: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is authoritative but costs a
264	  /// process for something two file reads answer.
265	  static func commonGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
266	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
267	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
268	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
269	      return nil
270	    }
271	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
272	    // A worktree's `.git` file: `gitdir: /abs/or/relative/path`.
273	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
274	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
275	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
276	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
277	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
278	    let gitDir =
279	      raw.hasPrefix("/")
280	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
281	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
282	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`.
283	    let parts = gitDir.standardized.pathComponents
284	    guard let index = parts.lastIndex(of: "worktrees"), index > 0 else { return gitDir }
285	    return URL(fileURLWithPath: "/" + parts[1..<index].joined(separator: "/"))
286	  }

288	  /// `FETCH_HEAD`'s modification time. git rewrites it on **every** fetch, no-ops included (verified),
289	  /// so its mtime is a complete record of git fetches — including one the user ran in a terminal.
290	  static func gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: URL?) -> VCSLastFetch {
291	    guard let dir = commonGitDir else { return .unknown }
292	    let head = dir.appendingPathComponent("FETCH_HEAD")
293	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: head.path) else { return .never }
294	    guard
295	      let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: head.path),
296	      let date = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
297	    else { return .unknown }
298	    return .at(date)
299	  }

312	  /// Exact two-way divergence, independent of the user's `push.default`.
313	  ///
314	  /// **Deliberately not `%(push:track)`/`%(upstream:track)`.** Under `push.default=simple` — git's
315	  /// built-in default — `%(push)` resolves to nothing for a branch with no upstream, and every
316	  /// workroom is `git worktree add -b`, i.e. has no upstream. Deriving counts from that field leaves
317	  /// the badge permanently blank on any machine not set to `push.default=current` (verified on git
318	  /// 2.55). It also sidesteps a branch whose `%(upstream)` is a *local* branch, which would otherwise
319	  /// produce counts against a ref that isn't on any remote.
320	  ///
321	  /// `A...B` with `--left-right --count` prints `<only in A>\t<only in B>`, so with `A = HEAD` the
322	  /// left number is ahead and the right is behind.
323	  static func gitCountsArgs(remote: String, branch: String) -> [String] {
324	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + [
325	      "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "HEAD...refs/remotes/\(remote)/\(branch)",
326	    ]
327	  }

330	  /// pass-NULL-and-honour-config philosophy `GitCommitDiff` documents. No `--no-write-fetch-head`
331	  /// either — `FETCH_HEAD` is exactly what `gitLastFetch` reads.
332	  /// `--` closes the option list. See `gitPushArgs` for why every builder in this file does that.

337	  /// `--set-upstream` only when there is no counterpart yet; passing it on every push would rewrite
338	  /// `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` each time. **Never** `--force`/`--force-with-lease`: a rejection
339	  /// becomes `.rejected` and the UI offers Pull.
340	  ///
341	  /// `--porcelain` is what makes the rejection detectable without reading prose — see
342	  /// `gitPushRejected(stdout:)`. It moves a machine-readable per-ref line onto stdout and leaves
343	  /// stderr's hints alone, so nothing else about the failure path changes.
344	  /// **The branch is sent as a fully-qualified refspec, never as a bare operand.** An argv array stops
345	  /// SHELL injection; it does nothing about OPTION injection, and git parses options that appear after
346	  /// the positional remote.
347	  ///
348	  /// The whole chain is verified on git 2.55, not theorised. `refs/heads/--all` is a legal refname
349	  /// (`check-ref-format` accepts it; only the `--branch` shorthand refuses). A malicious remote that
350	  /// points its `HEAD` at that ref makes `git clone` create a LOCAL branch called `--all`, which is what
351	  /// `git branch --show-current` and therefore `GitProvider.currentRef` then report. Feeding that to
352	  /// `push <remote> <branch>` pushed **every** branch in the repo to the attacker's server — measured:
353	  /// `refs/heads/--all`, `refs/heads/private-work-1`, `refs/heads/private-work-2`. Since every workroom
354	  /// of a project is a `git worktree add -b` in the same repo, that is every workroom's branch. `--mirror`
355	  /// is worse still: it can delete remote refs that are absent locally.
356	  ///
357	  /// A `refs/heads/…:refs/heads/…` refspec cannot present as an option no matter what the name contains,
358	  /// and it also pins the push to this one ref regardless of `push.default`. `--` alone would fix THIS
359	  /// builder, but not the pull one (see `gitPullArgs`), so both use refspecs for one rule.
360	  static func gitPushArgs(branch: String, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool) -> [String] {
361	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["push", "--porcelain"]
362	      + (setUpstream ? ["--set-upstream"] : [])
363	      + ["--", remote, "refs/heads/\(branch):refs/heads/\(branch)"]
364	  }

366	  /// Whether `push --porcelain` reported a rejected ref.
367	  ///
368	  /// Each porcelain line is `<flag>\t<from>:<to>\t<summary>`, and the flag is the contract: `!`
369	  /// rejected, ` ` updated, `*` new ref, `=` up to date, `-` deleted, `+` forced (we never force).
370	  ///
371	  /// This exists because the prose we used to match is translated and the flag is not. Homebrew git
372	  /// 2.55 under `fr_FR.UTF-8` answers `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées …` on stderr while stdout
373	  /// still reads `!\trefs/heads/master:refs/heads/master\t[rejected] (fetch first)` — measured, both
374	  /// locales. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C` so the prose match works today; this stops
375	  /// `.rejected` — the one failure whose recovery is a *different action* — depending on that pin.
376	  static func gitPushRejected(stdout: String) -> Bool {
377	    stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).contains { $0.hasPrefix("!\t") }
378	  }

416	  static func jjBookmarkListArgs() -> [String] {
417	    let template = """

551	  /// Parse `for-each-ref refs/remotes` output.
552	  ///
553	  /// Skips records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, whose short
554	  /// name is the bare remote and which would otherwise look like a branch called `origin`.
555	  /// Field count is checked rather than assumed: a ref name can't contain a control character, but
556	  /// being strict here means a malformed line is dropped rather than crashing the read.
557	  static func parseGitRemoteRefs(_ stdout: String) -> RemoteRefs {
558	    var remotes: [String] = []
559	    var shortNames: Set<String> = []
560	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
561	      let fields = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
562	      guard fields.count == 3 else { continue }
563	      guard fields[2].isEmpty else { continue }  // symref → origin/HEAD
564	      let refname = fields[0]
565	      let prefix = "refs/remotes/"
566	      guard refname.hasPrefix(prefix) else { continue }
567	      let short = String(refname.dropFirst(prefix.count))
568	      guard let slash = short.firstIndex(of: "/") else { continue }
569	      let remote = String(short[short.startIndex..<slash])
570	      guard !remote.isEmpty, slash < short.index(before: short.endIndex) else { continue }
571	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
572	      shortNames.insert(short)
573	    }
574	    return RemoteRefs(remotes: remotes, shortNames: shortNames)
575	  }

580	      .split(whereSeparator: { $0 == "\t" || $0 == " " })
581	    guard fields.count == 2, let ahead = Int(fields[0]), let behind = Int(fields[1]) else {

593	  /// Parse `bookmark list --all-remotes` output into per-name tracking, plus the remote names.
594	  ///
595	  /// **jj's counts are inverted relative to git and are swapped here.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an
596	  /// `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local*, which is git's **behind** — jj's own default
597	  /// template proves it by printing "ahead by N commits" next to `@origin`. One line, one comment, and
598	  /// a cross-backend integration test pins it.
599	  static func parseJJBookmarks(_ stdout: String) -> (bookmarks: [JJBookmark], remotes: [String]) {
600	    var remotes: [String] = []
601	    var trackingByName: [String: VCSTracking] = [:]
602	    var localNames: [String] = []
603	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
604	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
605	      guard f.count == 8 else { continue }
606	      let (name, remote) = (f[0], f[1])
607	      let present = f[3] == "1"
608	      let tracked = f[5] == "1"
609	      guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
610	      if remote.isEmpty {
611	        if !localNames.contains(name) { localNames.append(name) }
612	        continue
613	      }
614	      // A colocated repo exposes a pseudo-remote called `git` (jj's local git-tracking bookmarks).
615	      // It is not a remote, and including it would both pollute the remote list and produce counts
616	      // against the local git refs rather than a server.
617	      guard remote != "git" else { continue }
618	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
619	      // An untracked remote bookmark, or one deleted on the remote, cannot answer counts. `gone`
620	      // reports the deletion; nil counts report "unanswerable" rather than a misleading zero.
621	      let jjAhead = Int(f[6])
622	      let jjBehind = Int(f[7])
623	      trackingByName[name] = VCSTracking(
624	        comparedTo: "\(name)@\(remote)",
625	        ahead: tracked && present ? jjBehind : nil,  // swapped — see the doc comment
626	        behind: tracked && present ? jjAhead : nil,
627	        gone: !present)
628	    }
629	    let bookmarks = localNames.map { JJBookmark(name: $0, tracking: trackingByName[$0]) }
630	    return (bookmarks, remotes)
631	  }

653	  /// Map a failed command to a typed failure. `nil` means success.
654	  ///
655	  /// `gitDir` lets a failed pull be upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` — the distinction matters because
656	  /// that state must offer Abort, not Retry.
657	  static func classify(
658	    _ result: CommandResult, action: VCSRemoteAction, tool: String,
659	    gitDir: URL? = nil
660	  ) -> VCSRemoteFailure? {
661	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .toolMissing(tool) }
662	    let err = result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout
663	    // A timed-out pull may have left a rebase behind; that reads better than "timed out".
664	    if result.timedOut {
665	      if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
666	      return .timedOut(action)
667	    }
668	    guard !result.ok else { return nil }
669	    if err.contains("Host key verification failed") || err.contains("REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION") {
670	      return .hostKeyUnverified(err)
671	    }
672	    if err.contains("terminal prompts disabled") || err.contains("could not read Username")
673	      || err.contains("could not read Password") || err.contains("Authentication failed")
674	      || err.contains("Permission denied (publickey)")
675	    {
676	      return .authRequired(err)
677	    }
678	    if err.contains("would be overwritten") { return .dirtyWorkingTree(err) }
679	    if err.contains("does not appear to be a git repository") || err.contains("No such remote")
680	      || err.contains("no such remote") || err.contains("No git remotes")
681	    {
682	      return .noRemote
683	    }
684	    // Flag column first, prose second. The string checks stay as a fallback rather than being replaced:
685	    // `--porcelain` is ours to pass on the push path only, so a rejection surfaced by any other route
686	    // (a remote helper, a future caller that forgets the flag) still classifies.
687	    if gitPushRejected(stdout: result.stdout) || err.contains("Updates were rejected")
688	      || err.contains("! [rejected]")
689	    {
690	      return .rejected(err)
691	    }
692	    // Both jj-only, and both permanent until the user acts — so they must NOT reach `.other`, whose
693	    // recovery is a retry of the same doomed command. jj doesn't localize, so matching its prose is safe
694	    // here in a way it wouldn't be for git.
695	    if err.contains("since it has no description") || err.contains("has no description") {
696	      return .needsDescription(err)
697	    }
698	    if err.contains("is immutable") || err.contains("immutable commits") {
699	      return .immutableHistory(err)
700	    }
701	    if err.contains("Failed to take lock for Git import/export")
702	      || (err.contains(".lock")
703	        && (err.contains("could not be obtained") || err.contains("File exists")
704	          || err.contains("Unable to create")))
705	    {
706	      return .locked(lockFile(in: err))
707	    }
708	    if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
709	    // A lock failure that never names a lock. git's message depends on WHICH internal step hit the lock:
710	    // a fast-forward pull reports `Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`, but a pull that must really
711	    // rebase fails in autostash first and says only `error: could not write index` / `fatal: Cannot
712	    // autostash` — no path, no "lock", nothing the checks above can match. That is the diverged pull,
713	    // i.e. exactly what the toolbar's Pull button is for, and it was landing in `.other` with raw stderr.
714	    //
715	    // So when the symptoms are lock-shaped, ask the DISK instead of the message. Deliberately last: any
716	    // failure git explains properly keeps its own classification, and this only speaks for the ones it
717	    // doesn't.
718	    if lockSymptom(err), let lock = existingLockFile(gitDir: gitDir) { return .locked(lock) }
719	    let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
720	    return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
721	  }

726	    guard let gitDir else { return false }

732	  /// The lock file a failure is complaining about, or nil if we can't point at one.
733	  ///
734	  /// The path is taken from git's OWN message rather than guessed: git names the exact file it couldn't
735	  /// create (`fatal: Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`), and a repo has several lock files that
736	  /// mean different things — `index.lock`, `packed-refs.lock`, `HEAD.lock`, `config.lock`. Naming the
737	  /// wrong one would send someone to delete a file that isn't the problem.
738	  ///
739	  /// Returns nil for jj's import/export lock, whose message carries no path, and — deliberately — when
740	  /// the named file no longer exists: a lock that cleared between the failure and this check WAS
741	  /// transient contention, which is exactly the case where Retry is the right offer.
742	  static func lockFile(in stderr: String) -> VCSLockFile? {
743	    guard let path = parseLockPath(stderr) else { return nil }
744	    guard let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: path),
745	      let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
746	    else { return nil }
747	    return VCSLockFile(path: path, modifiedAt: modified)

753	  /// that doesn't print the lock's name; anything broader would start blaming a lock file that happens to
754	  /// exist for failures it had nothing to do with.
755	  static func lockSymptom(_ stderr: String) -> Bool {
756	    stderr.contains("could not write index") || stderr.contains("Cannot autostash")
757	      || stderr.contains("cannot lock ref") || stderr.contains("Unable to write")
758	  }

761	  /// own git dir; `packed-refs.lock` and `config.lock` live in the COMMON dir that every worktree shares.
762	  static let knownLockNames = ["index.lock", "packed-refs.lock", "HEAD.lock", "config.lock"]

764	  /// The first lock file actually present in this repo, checking both the worktree's git dir and the
765	  /// common one — a workroom is a `git worktree`, so its `index.lock` and the repo's `packed-refs.lock`
766	  /// are in different directories.
767	  static func existingLockFile(gitDir: URL?) -> VCSLockFile? {
768	    guard let gitDir else { return nil }
769	    let fm = FileManager.default
770	    var dirs = [gitDir]
771	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`. Cheap and string-only; `commonGitDir` does the same trip
772	    // from a path rather than from an already-resolved git dir.
773	    if gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().lastPathComponent == "worktrees" {
774	      dirs.append(gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent())
775	    }
776	    for dir in dirs {
777	      for name in knownLockNames {
778	        let candidate = dir.appendingPathComponent(name)
779	        guard let attrs = try? fm.attributesOfItem(atPath: candidate.path),
780	          let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
781	        else { continue }
782	        return VCSLockFile(path: candidate.path, modifiedAt: modified)
783	      }
784	    }
785	    return nil
786	  }

788	  /// The quoted path out of git's lock errors. Pure, so the parsing is testable without a repo.
789	  ///
790	  /// Covers both phrasings that quote a path — the bare `Unable to create '<path>'` and the ref-update
791	  /// form (`error: cannot lock ref 'refs/…': Unable to create '<path>.lock': File exists`), which nests
792	  /// two quoted strings and must yield the second.
793	  static func parseLockPath(_ stderr: String) -> String? {
794	    guard let marker = stderr.range(of: "Unable to create '") else { return nil }
795	    let rest = stderr[marker.upperBound...]
796	    guard let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "'") else { return nil }
797	    let path = String(rest[..<close])
798	    // Only ever report an absolute path to a `.lock`: a relative one would be meaningless to a user
799	    // reading it out of a tooltip, and a non-`.lock` match means the phrasing wasn't what we assumed.
800	    guard path.hasPrefix("/"), path.hasSuffix(".lock") else { return nil }
801	    return path
802	  }

804	  /// This worktree's OWN git directory — `<common>/worktrees/<name>` for a workroom, the same as the
805	  /// common dir for a project root. Rebase state (`rebase-merge`), `HEAD` and `index` live here, unlike
806	  /// `FETCH_HEAD` which `commonGitDir` deliberately resolves to the shared copy.
807	  static func worktreeGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
808	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
809	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
810	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
811	      return nil
812	    }
813	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
814	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
815	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
816	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
817	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
818	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
819	    return raw.hasPrefix("/")
820	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
821	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
822	  }

863	  private func gitRemoteState(path: String, current: VCSRef) async -> VCSRemoteResolution {
864	    let refs = await run(Self.gitRemoteRefsArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
865	    if let failure = Self.classify(refs, action: .fetch, tool: "git") {
866	      // A blip must not blank a good toolbar; a missing tool or a real error should show.
867	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
868	      return .failed(failure)
869	    }
870	    let parsed = Self.parseGitRemoteRefs(refs.stdout)
871	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(parsed.remotes)
872	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
873	    if let primary, let branch = current.name, current.kind == .branch {
874	      let counterpart = "\(primary)/\(branch)"
875	      if parsed.shortNames.contains(counterpart) {
876	        let counts = await run(
877	          Self.gitCountsArgs(remote: primary, branch: branch), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
878	        if let parsedCounts = Self.parseCounts(counts.stdout) {
879	          tracking = VCSTracking(
880	            comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: parsedCounts.ahead, behind: parsedCounts.behind,
881	            gone: false)
882	        } else {
883	          tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: false)
884	        }
885	      } else {
886	        // No counterpart on the remote — the normal state of a fresh workroom, since
887	        // `git worktree add -b` sets no upstream. Reported as `gone` so the toolbar offers Publish.
888	        tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: true)
889	      }
890	    }
891	    return .state(
892	      VCSRemoteState(
893	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: parsed.remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
894	        lastFetch: Self.gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: Self.commonGitDir(at: path)),
895	        resolvedAt: Date()))
896	  }

898	  private func jjRemoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef) async
899	    -> VCSRemoteResolution
900	  {
901	    // Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated.
902	    let list = await run(Self.jjBookmarkListArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
903	    if let failure = Self.classify(list, action: .fetch, tool: "jj") {
904	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
905	      return .failed(failure)
906	    }
907	    let parsed = Self.parseJJBookmarks(list.stdout)
908	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(parsed.remotes)
909	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
910	    if let primary {
911	      switch current.kind {
912	      case .branch:
913	        tracking = current.name.flatMap { name in
914	          parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }?.tracking
915	        }
916	      // `.none` belongs with `.ancestor`, and leaving it out was a bug that hid the exact case this
917	      // toolbar exists for. `jj git fetch` fast-forwards a tracked local bookmark, so as soon as the
918	      // main line moves, an unbookmarked `@`'s ancestry contains no bookmark at all and `currentRef`
919	      // drops from `.ancestor` to `.none`. Sending that to `tracking = nil` meant the counts, the pills
920	      // and `canPull` all vanished at the moment the workroom first became behind — the toolbar went
921	      // quiet precisely when it had something to say. The revsets below never needed a bookmark to
922	      // begin with; `.detached` still yields nil, since that's git's shape and has no jj meaning.
923	      case .ancestor, .none:
924	        // `@` carries no bookmark — the normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates
925	        // no bookmark. The bookmark row's counts would describe the ANCESTOR, not the user's work, so
926	        // count the actual revsets instead. The two are deliberately scoped differently: ahead against
927	        // every remote bookmark (anything already pushed anywhere isn't ahead), behind against `trunk()`
928	        // alone (see `jjBehindRevset` — the all-bookmarks form counted other branches' work as ours to
929	        // pull). Both agree with what the buttons do: `jjPushRevision` and `jjRebaseDestination`.
930	        let ahead = await run(
931	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjAheadRevset(remote: primary)), in: path, timeout: refTimeout
932	        )
933	        let behind = await run(
934	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjBehindRevset), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
935	        tracking = VCSTracking(
936	          comparedTo: primary,
937	          ahead: ahead.ok ? Self.countLines(ahead.stdout) : nil,
938	          behind: behind.ok ? Self.countLines(behind.stdout) : nil,
939	          gone: false)
940	      case .detached:
941	        tracking = nil
942	      }
943	    }
944	    // jj's fetch is invisible to `FETCH_HEAD` (it passes `--no-write-fetch-head`), so scan the op log.
945	    let ops = await run(Self.jjOpLogArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
946	    let lastFetch = ops.ok ? Self.parseJJFetchOp(ops.stdout) : nil
947	    return .state(
948	      VCSRemoteState(
949	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: parsed.remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
950	        lastFetch: lastFetch.map { .at($0) } ?? (ops.ok ? .never : .unknown),
951	        resolvedAt: Date()))
952	  }

1018	  func pullRebase(
1019	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
1020	    tracking: VCSTracking?
1021	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult {
1022	    // Both backends fetch first, at the project root, for the reasons `opDirectory` documents. For git
1023	    // `pull` would fetch too, but doing it explicitly at the root keeps `FETCH_HEAD` — and so the
1024	    // "last fetched" label — correct for every workroom of the project.
1025	    // Hoisted above the fetch: BOTH steps classify against it, since a lock can block either one.
1026	    let gitDir = Self.worktreeGitDir(at: path)
1027	    let fetchDir = Self.opDirectory(.fetch, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1028	    let fetchArgs =
1029	      vcs == "jj" ? Self.jjFetchArgs(remote: remote) : Self.gitFetchArgs(remote: remote)
1030	    guard
1031	      let fetched = await gated(
1032	        projectRoot,
1033	        { [self] in
1034	          await run(fetchArgs, in: fetchDir, timeout: fetchTimeout, network: true)
1035	        })
1036	    else { return .failed(.other("pull was cancelled")) }
1037	    if let failure = Self.classify(fetched, action: .pull, tool: vcs, gitDir: gitDir) {
1038	      return .failed(failure)
1039	    }
1040	
1041	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.pull, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1042	    let args: [String]
1043	    if vcs == "jj" {
1044	      // Always rebases now. An unbookmarked `@` falls back to `trunk()` rather than returning early:
1045	      // fetching moves the remote bookmarks but does NOT move `@`, so stopping there left the workroom
1046	      // as far behind as it started while the toolbar went on offering Pull. Already a descendant of the
1047	      // destination is not an error — jj prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
1048	      args = Self.jjRebaseArgs(
1049	        onto: Self.jjRebaseDestination(comparedTo: tracking?.comparedTo, remote: remote))
1050	    } else {
1051	      guard let branch = Self.pullBranch(current: current, tracking: tracking) else {
1052	        return .failed(.other("no remote branch to pull from."))
1053	      }
1054	      args = Self.gitPullArgs(remote: remote, branch: branch)
1055	    }
1056	    guard
1057	      let result = await gated(
1058	        projectRoot,
1059	        { [self] in
1060	          await run(args, in: dir, timeout: pullTimeout, network: true)
1061	        })
1062	    else { return .failed(.other("pull was cancelled")) }
1063	    if let failure = Self.classify(result, action: .pull, tool: vcs, gitDir: gitDir) {
1064	      return .failed(failure)
1065	    }
1066	    return .ok(summary: "Pulled from \(remote)")
1067	  }

1069	  /// The remote branch a pull rebases from: the counterpart's own name, stripped of its `<remote>/`
1070	  /// prefix, falling back to the local branch name (the same-name convention).
1071	  static func pullBranch(current: VCSRef, tracking: VCSTracking?) -> String? {
1072	    if let comparedTo = tracking?.comparedTo, let slash = comparedTo.firstIndex(of: "/") {
1073	      return String(comparedTo[comparedTo.index(after: slash)...])
1074	    }
1075	    return current.name
1076	  }

1078	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult {
1079	    guard vcs != "jj" else {
1080	      // jj's rebase is atomic and undoable — there is no half-finished state to abort.
1081	      return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort")
1082	    }
1083	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.abortRebase, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1084	    guard
1085	      let result = await gated(

1091	    if let failure = Self.classify(result, action: .abortRebase, tool: vcs) {

1093	    }
1094	    return .ok(summary: "Rebase aborted")

118	  private static func resolve(
119	    state: VCSRemoteState?, hasTarget: Bool, toolsUsable: Bool,
120	    activity: VCSSyncActivity, failure: VCSRemoteFailure?,
121	    lastAction: VCSRemoteAction?, pullRebase: Bool, pullConflicted: Bool,
122	    now: Date
123	  ) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
124	    // [13] A failure outranks everything: it's the only state with something to recover from, and
125	    // burying it under a count would leave the user with no idea the action didn't happen.
126	    if let failure, case .idle = activity {
127	      let message = describe(failure)
128	      let recovery = retryAction(for: failure, lastAction: lastAction)
129	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
130	        // With no recovery to offer, the title must not read as a button. "Retry" over a failure that
131	        // cannot be retried is the whole defect this branch fixes.
132	        //
133	        // The title names the RECOVERY, not the action that failed. It used to read `lastAction?.label`
134	        // while `action:` below was `recovery` — so a rejected push rendered a button labelled "Push"
135	        // that performed a Pull. The two must be the same verb or the button lies about what it does.
136	        titleVariants: recovery.map { [$0.label] } ?? [],
137	        subtitle: message, subtitleShort: message,
138	        symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill",
139	        action: recovery,
140	        isEnabled: recovery != nil,
141	        // The tooltip is where a failure gets room to explain itself — one line fits the bar, the
142	        // remedy usually doesn't.
143	        tone: .failure, help: explain(failure, now: now),
144	        accessibility: "\(lastAction?.label ?? "Action") failed. \(explain(failure, now: now))",
145	        lockPath: lockPath(of: failure))
146	    }
147	
148	    // [10/11/12] In flight — one action at a time, so this can't collide with a second.
149	    if case .running(let action) = activity {
150	      let title: String
151	      let subtitle: String
152	      switch action {
153	      case .fetch: (title, subtitle) = ("Fetching…", "from \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
154	      case .push: (title, subtitle) = ("Pushing…", "to \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
155	      case .pull: (title, subtitle) = ("Pulling…", "from \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
156	      case .abortRebase: (title, subtitle) = ("Aborting…", "rebase")
157	      }
158	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
159	        titleVariants: [title], subtitle: subtitle, subtitleShort: subtitle,
160	        symbol: nil, badge: badge(ahead: state?.tracking?.ahead),
161	        action: nil, isEnabled: false, help: "\(title) \(subtitle)",

165	    // [14] The pull we ran landed conflicts.

171	    //

180	        "The rebase completed with conflicts. Resolve them in this workroom — the Changes list marks "

287	  /// Which action a failure offers. `.rebaseInProgress` deliberately offers **Abort**, never a retry —
288	  /// a retry fails identically until the rebase is cleared. `.toolMissing` offers nothing, because no
289	  /// click can fix a missing binary.
290	  /// **Exhaustive on purpose — no `default:`.** It used to end `default: return lastAction`, so every
291	  /// failure added later silently inherited "offer a retry", which is the exact defect the `[13]` tier
292	  /// exists to prevent. Two of the failures below were added precisely because they are permanent, and a
293	  /// `default:` would have handed them a doomed button without a compile error.
294	  static func retryAction(for failure: VCSRemoteFailure, lastAction: VCSRemoteAction?)
295	    -> VCSRemoteAction?
296	  {
297	    switch failure {
298	    case .rebaseInProgress: return .abortRebase
299	    case .rejected: return .pull  // the fix for a rejection is to pull, never to force
300	    case .toolMissing, .noRemote: return nil
301	    // Permanent until the user does something outside Workroom: describe the commit, or move off a base
302	    // whose history is protected. Retrying either runs the identical command and fails identically.
303	    case .needsDescription, .immutableHistory: return nil
304	    case .timedOut, .authRequired, .hostKeyUnverified, .dirtyWorkingTree, .other:
305	      return lastAction
306	    // A LOCATED lock file offers nothing, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the file is sitting there, so
307	    // every retry fails identically and the button is a promise that can't be kept. Removing it is the
308	    // only fix and Workroom won't do that for you (see `VCSRemoteFailure.locked`), so the recovery is
309	    // explained rather than offered. An unlocatable lock was transient contention — retry away.
310	    case .locked(let file): return file == nil ? lastAction : nil
311	    }

Based on my review of the changed files (VCSWriting.swift, VCSSyncPresentation.swift, VCSToolbar.swift, AppStore.swift, and the four test files), this is a macOS SwiftUI app diff that adjusts:

1. **stderr classification** — two new jj-specific failure cases (`needsDescription`, `immutableHistory`) matched by substring on stderr. Raw stderr is carried in the enum payload but only used for pattern-matching; `describe()`/`explain()` return hardcoded strings for both, so the payload never reaches the UI.
2. **retry-action exhaustiveness** — the `default:` case is removed. Every existing case is enumerated, so behavior is unchanged for known cases and future additions produce a compile error rather than a silent "retry the doomed command" default. Safer than before.
3. **`busyElsewhere` disable flag** — pure UI clickability gate applied AFTER the ladder; disables the button when another workroom holds the model-wide `inFlight` lock. Fail-closed (no action, disabled). `perform` was already the enforcement point.
4. **`handleRemoteMutation` refactor** — skips the forced app-wide sweep for `.fetch`, uses per-selection debounced refresh; `noteConflictState` still re-verifies `sid` so a moved selection no-ops.
5. **`refresh(force:true) → refresh()` on app activation** — respects TTL. No security control was riding on the forced bypass.
6. **Test hygiene** — `Defaults.reset(.vcsLastFetch)` in setUp too, to avoid cross-class parallel-worker contamination of a persisted defaults dict.

Sinks I verified:
- Command args (`gitPushArgs`/`gitPullArgs`/jj variants) unchanged — the existing refspec + `--` boundary defense against option injection is intact.
- The new stderr matches (`"has no description"`, `"is immutable"`) are ordered AFTER `.rejected`, so a rejected git push with a colliding branch name in porcelain output still classifies as rejected. Worst-case misclassification of a git error into a jj-only case yields "no retry offered" — a UX quirk, not a security defect.
- No new logging/telemetry sink; the raw `err` in the two new failure payloads is never rendered.
- No new filesystem/exec/network path introduced.

No exploitable defects found.
